messages.author: 6e42dc87c8b5766f
messages.subject: Detection History records being removed
parts:
Hello,

Thank you for developing camtrapR, I have a question regarding "detectionHistory".

This is my input: 
DetHist1 <-camtrapR::detectionHistory(recordTable = rec.db.species0,
                                      camOp = camop_hours,
                                      stationCol = "Station",
                                      speciesCol = "Species",
                                      recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                      species = "NHM",
                                      occasionLength = 1,
                                      day1="survey",
                                      includeEffort = F,
                                      output = "count",
                                      datesAsOccasionNames=T)

I get the following warnings:
At 30 stations there were records after camera operation date range:  B1, B13, B15, B16, B17, B2, B21, B22, B23, B24, B25, B26, B27, B28, B29, B3, B30, B32, B33, B37, B38, B39, B43, B44, B5, B54, B55, B56, B8, U51
355 records (out of 23560) were removed because they were taken after the end of the last occasion, e.g.:
B1: 2022-03-02 00:26:32
B1: 2022-03-02 00:26:37
B1: 2022-03-02 00:26:43
B1: 2022-03-02 00:27:10
B1: 2022-03-02 00:27:15
B1: 2022-03-02 00:27:20

This is confusing (and causing the output counts to be incorrect) because the records that are being removed are not after the end of the last occasion, they are on the day of retrieval. For example, at B1 the last occasion is 2022-03-01+19h_2022-03-02+19h with the retrievalCol being 2022-03-02 07:00:00, but only the records up to 2022-03-01 23:59:59 are being counted, with any past that time being removed. Is there something I can do to fix this?

Many thanks,
Kiarrah

I have the occasion start time as 12, with an occasion length of 1. The records that are being removed are all on the same day as 'Retrieval Date' but occur before 12. (08:44; 01:36; and 04:30). 

Are there any workarounds for this? I would like to keep the occasion start time as-is because it makes the most sense for my focal species. I have very few detections to begin with so losing 3 would really affect analysis.

Thanks for your help!

Amy

messages.subject: Re: Detection History records being removed
parts:
Hi,

I am wondering if there was a resolution to this? I am facing similar issues with my dataset. The code is:

dh_dhl <- detectionHistory(
  recordTable = Rtable,
  species = 'Dhole',
  camOp = camopsf,
  output = "binary",

recordDateTimeCol = "DT_new",
  recordDateTimeFormat = "dmy HM",
  occasionLength = 1,
  maxNumberDays = 16,
  day1 = "station",
  includeEffort = TRUE,
  scaleEffort = FALSE,
  datesAsOccasionNames = FALSE,
  timeZone = "Asia/Kolkata",
  writecsv = FALSE,
  outDir = getwd()
)

the error is:
Error in if (last_col_to_keep2[yyy] + 1 < ncol(cam.op)) { :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:

At 12 stations there were records after camera operation date range:  VP-12, VP-15, VP-33, VP-35, VP-28, VP-41, VP-22, VP-23, VP-29, VP-31, VP-32, VP-49

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Now, I am not sure what the first error means.

Next, the stations highlighted above are the only ones with records of my species of interest and they fall well within the camera operation date range - this is also reflective in the camera operation matrix. The dates are in dmy HM format in both the record table and camera operation matrix. 

Reference screenshots of camera operation matrix (h1) and record table (2) attached. Please note that in station VP-12, for example, there is one record of dhole (species of interest) on 28.01.2023 and the camera trap was active between 23.01.2023 to 03.02.2023. Yet the error message suggests that the record was after camera operation date range! 

I have already tried changing the date time formats to ymd for both, but the error persists.

To ensure that the issue is not with the DateTimeOriginal column, I also tried reassembling the dates and times in a new column DT_new, but the issue persists. 

I am not sure how R is misinterpreting the dates and times. I would really appreciate some help. 

Thanks,
Divyajyoti
